name: NVDLA v1 control and datapath
summary: An NPU architecture map with executable CSB acceptance, selected register-bank protection, and two interrupt mask lanes. The convolution, activation, pooling, and memory engines are documented architectural context, not a simulated neural network.

sources.title: NVDLA Hardware Architectural Specification
sources.locator: Functional Description; Configuration space bus; Host interrupt; Ping-pong Synchronization Mechanism

sources.title: NVDLA Integrator's Manual
sources.locator: Hardware System Interface; Configuration Interface; Clock and reset interface

groups.label: Host and control
groups.description: Low-bandwidth register programming and completion notification. Acceptance outputs describe the current sampling cycle, not an entire transaction history.

groups.label: CSB request channel
groups.description: Valid and ready jointly accept a request. Read and non-posted write requests require responses; posted writes do not.

groups.label: Ping-pong register banks
groups.description: PRODUCER selects a duplicated register bank; writes to an enabled bank are ignored. Enable-state snapshots are supplied as inputs.

groups.label: Completion interrupts
groups.description: Two representative status/mask lanes. All other interrupt status bits are assumed clear.

groups.label: Convolution pipeline
groups.description: Convolution DMA, buffer, sequencer, MAC array, and accumulator. Their arithmetic and scheduling are not executed in this model.

groups.label: Post-processing engines
groups.description: SDP activation and PDP pooling context. Optional engines and operating modes depend on the generated IP configuration.

groups.label: Memory interfaces
groups.description: Main memory interface, external DRAM, and optional SRAM interface. Physical memory and bus timing are not modeled.

inputs.label: CSB request valid
inputs.description: Host presents a stable CSB request for the current sampling cycle.

inputs.label: CSB receiver ready
inputs.description: Observed accelerator ready signal. Backpressure generation is external to this control contract.

inputs.label: Write request
inputs.description: CSB write flag; false denotes a read.

inputs.label: Non-posted write
inputs.description: Request write completion for a write transaction. This field does not turn a read into a write.

inputs.label: PRODUCER selects bank 1
inputs.description: Snapshot of the software-controlled register-bank selector.

inputs.label: Bank 0 enabled
inputs.description: Snapshot of bank 0 D_OP_ENABLE. Enabled means pending or executing, not necessarily currently running.

inputs.label: Bank 1 enabled
inputs.description: Snapshot of bank 1 D_OP_ENABLE. Hardware clearing and layer execution are outside this contract.

inputs.label: Interrupt status lane 0
inputs.description: One representative GLB interrupt-status bit, provided by the surrounding accelerator.

inputs.label: Mask interrupt lane 0
inputs.description: True masks this status bit. NVDLA mask polarity is not STM32 IMR polarity.

inputs.label: Interrupt status lane 1
inputs.description: A second representative GLB status bit. Other unrepresented bits are assumed zero.

inputs.label: Mask interrupt lane 1
inputs.description: True prevents this lane from asserting the host interrupt.

blocks.label: CSB acceptance
blocks.description: A request transfers only when valid AND ready are asserted together.

blocks.label: Read response required
blocks.description: An accepted read requires one ordered read response later. This is an obligation, not the response-valid signal.

blocks.label: Write completion required
blocks.description: Only accepted non-posted writes request a write completion. No completion latency is invented.

blocks.label: Posted write accepted
blocks.description: A posted write is accepted without a requested completion response.

blocks.label: Selected bank protected
blocks.description: Choose the enable bit using PRODUCER, not the datapath CONSUMER pointer.

blocks.label: Bank write allowed
blocks.description: For a write addressed to this duplicated configuration bank, accept parameter changes only while that bank is disabled.

blocks.label: Protected write ignored
blocks.description: An enabled duplicated bank ignores writes even when the layer is only pending. This is not a bus-error or a missing-acknowledgement model.

blocks.label: Unmasked status 0
blocks.description: A status bit contributes to IRQ only if its mask bit is zero.

blocks.label: Unmasked status 1
blocks.description: The independent second interrupt lane obeys the same mask polarity.

blocks.label: Host interrupt
blocks.description: OR of the two represented unmasked status bits. All other bits are assumed clear.

blocks.label: Convolution DMA
blocks.description: Fetches convolution features and weights via the memory system.
blocks.reason: No DMA addresses, transaction queues, or data values are executed.

blocks.label: Convolution buffer
blocks.description: Local feature and weight storage shared by the convolution pipeline.
blocks.reason: Capacity and banking vary with the generated IP configuration; no capacity or storage contents are assumed.

blocks.label: Convolution sequencer
blocks.description: Schedules convolution operands from the buffer toward MAC execution.
blocks.reason: Tensor shapes, scheduling, and layer dependency enforcement are not simulated.

blocks.label: Convolution MAC array
blocks.description: Configurable multiply-accumulate resources, shown as one aggregated architectural block.
blocks.reason: Not a fixed MAC count, precision support matrix, or executed convolution.

blocks.label: Convolution accumulator
blocks.description: Accumulates and prepares convolution results for subsequent processing.
blocks.reason: Accumulator widths, saturation, rounding, and arithmetic values are not modeled.

blocks.label: SDP activation engine
blocks.description: Single data point processing: activation, scaling, and element-wise operations where configured.
blocks.reason: The architecture is represented; no neural activation function is evaluated.

blocks.label: PDP pooling engine
blocks.description: Planar data processor for configured pooling operations.
blocks.reason: Availability depends on the generated configuration; no pooling result or throughput is produced.

blocks.label: Main memory interface
blocks.description: NVDLA's main data interface connects to system memory through the SoC interconnect.
blocks.reason: Memory response ordering and AXI burst transactions are not executed here.

blocks.label: System DRAM
blocks.description: External system-context memory supplying weights, features, and outputs.
blocks.reason: Memory technology, size, latency, and bandwidth belong to the integrating SoC and remain unspecified.

blocks.label: Optional SRAM interface
blocks.description: An optional second memory interface for an integrating system's SRAM.
blocks.reason: Shown as optional capability, not a mandatory feature of every NVDLA build.

connections.label: Layer configuration
connections.description: Logical software configuration relationship; does not start a simulated DMA.

connections.label: System memory path
connections.description: Conceptual data path through the main interface, not a sampled bus signal.

connections.label: Feature and weight reads
connections.description: The convolution DMA accesses memory through the memory subsystem.

connections.label: Feature and weight buffers
connections.description: First part of the documented convolution core pipeline.

connections.label: Buffered operands
connections.description: Logical operand flow from storage to the sequencer.

connections.label: Scheduled operands
connections.description: Logical flow in the documented convolution pipeline.

connections.label: Fused processing path
connections.description: A possible fused path; independent mode instead uses memory traffic.

connections.label: Optional fused pooling
connections.description: Logical path when the corresponding engines and mode are enabled.

connections.label: Output storage
connections.description: Architectural store path, not a memory timing prediction.

connections.label: Optional SRAM access
connections.description: Alternative data interface when generated and integrated.

outputs.label: Request accepted
outputs.description: A transfer condition, not a completion response.

outputs.label: Read response owed
outputs.description: Obligation arising from the current accepted request.

outputs.label: Bank write allowed
outputs.description: Permission for the addressed duplicated register bank only.

outputs.label: Host IRQ asserted
outputs.description: Two-lane mask reduction with all other status bits zero.

requirements.text: A request transfers exactly when valid and ready are both asserted.
Accepted reads and non-posted writes create separate response obligations; posted writes do not request completion.
An enabled duplicated bank ignores writes regardless of whether it is currently running or only pending.
With other lanes clear, host interrupt is the OR of status AND NOT mask for the represented lanes.

assumptions: Each input update represents stable interface/register snapshots at a sampling point; no CSB clocks, resets, or outstanding-response queue are emulated.
Bank protection applies to an addressed duplicated parameter bank. Address decode and all other CSB targets are outside this contract.
The two interrupt lanes are representative and unnamed; every other GLB status bit is zero.
Architectural connections show possible logical relationships, never live data. Optional SRAM and pooling capabilities are not guaranteed in every generated NVDLA configuration.
omissions: Neural-network execution, MAC/accumulator arithmetic, quantization, tensor storage, scheduling, and performance.
Actual D_OP_ENABLE state transitions, clock-domain crossing, reset synchronization, all CSB addresses and response payloads, and complete interrupt state.
Full RTL equivalence, synthesis, place-and-route, physical floorplan, silicon validation, and SKU-specific counts.
